- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above recent peak for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, model overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% for 3–7 days ahead.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) and price is stable or declining, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast by 1–4% for next 5–10 days.
- Model often fails to capture mean reversion in 10–15 day horizons; if price is above 30-day moving average, reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.00) and price is falling, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–7 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 5–7 days); apply downward correction of 1–4% for first 5 days.
